*Kusalattika, Atītattikadvaya* is a canonical Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna* collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Within the intricate combinatory structure of the *Paṭṭhāna*, this section analyzes conditional relations by pairing the triad of wholesome states (*kusalattika*) with the pair of past triads (*atītattikadvaya*) [SuttaCentral].

No curated parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are reported, and computational analysis records no cross-language matches meeting significance thresholds [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, however, automated text-reuse analysis demonstrates that the text shares extensive formulaic material with other sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, exhibiting 110 matching passages across 35 other texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal overlaps occur with the *Kusalattika, Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 16.25), spanning 12 matches totaling 3,397 shared characters (including §3.1–4.1 matching §20.1–21.1), and the *Kusalattika, Āsavagocchaka* (Patthana 22.6), with 10 matches totaling 3,224 characters [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits close structural alignment with related triads, notably the *Kusalattika, Ajjhattattikadvaya* (Patthana 23.18), with which it shares segments §0.1–4.1, as well as the *Kusalattika, Vitakkattika* (Patthana 23.5) and *Kusalattika, Ajjhattattikadvaya* (Patthana 17.19) [DharmaNexus].

The text does not appear individually cited or discussed in the consulted secondary research literature [SuttaCentral].
